title: Aloo Gobi
subtitle: Dry potato and cauliflower curry
excerpt: The classic Indian vegetable combination of potato and cauliflower cooked with whole spices, ginger, garlic, and tomato until completely tender and dry. Simple and deeply flavoured.

recipe.sourceNotes: Aloo gobi is one of the most widely eaten vegetable dishes in north India, Pakistan, and the Indian diaspora worldwide. The name simply means potato (aloo) and cauliflower (gobi) in Hindi and Punjabi. It is a dry dish, cooked without added liquid: the vegetables steam in their own moisture and the spiced oil. It is a staple of everyday home cooking across north India and became one of the most popular vegetable dishes in British-Indian restaurants.

content.text: Aloo gobi is a dry dish. No water or stock goes in; the vegetables cook in the spiced oil, steaming in the moisture they release. Keep the lid on for the first 10 minutes, then remove it and cook over a higher heat to dry and caramelise the edges. The potato and cauliflower should be slightly catching by the end, not wet or soupy.
Heat the oil in a large wide pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, and chilli. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the turmeric, coriander, and cumin. Stir for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.

Add the potato chunks and stir to coat in the spice mixture. Season with salt. Lay the cauliflower florets on top. Cover with a lid and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, checking and stirring every 5 minutes, until both vegetables are tender.

Remove the lid, increase the heat to medium-high, and cook for 5 more minutes, tossing, until the vegetables are slightly coloured at the edges. Add the garam masala and stir through. Scatter with coriander and serve.
